subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT present in animal cells?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chloroplast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chloroplasts** are **absent in animal cells**. These organelles are specific to plant cells and some algae, where they are responsible for **photosynthesis**, a process that converts light energy into chemical energy stored as glucose.
 
• Animal cells do not perform photosynthesis as they obtain energy by consuming organic matter rather than producing it. *Hence, chloroplasts are absent in animal cells.*
 
• **Nucleus**, **plasma membrane**, and **cytoplasm** are present in both animal and plant cells. These are essential components for cellular function. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*
 
• The **nucleus** houses the genetic material (DNA) and controls cellular activities, making it an indispensable organelle in all eukaryotic cells.
 
• The **plasma membrane**, also known as the cell membrane, surrounds the cell, providing structural support, protection, and regulating the movement of substances in and out of the cell.
 
• The **cytoplasm** is the jelly-like substance filling the cell, where various metabolic processes and organelle activities take place. It is present in all cell types.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chloroplast:**

 
 
• Chloroplasts are double-membrane-bound organelles found in plant cells and certain protists like algae.
 
• They contain the pigment **chlorophyll**, which captures light energy for photosynthesis.
 
• Chloroplasts have their own DNA and ribosomes, enabling them to produce some of their own proteins.
 
• They are responsible for converting light energy into glucose and oxygen, which are essential for the survival of plants and indirectly for all living organisms.
 
 
 
• **Nucleus:**
 
 
• The nucleus is a membrane-bound organelle present in all eukaryotic cells.
 
• It contains the cell's genetic material in the form of DNA, organized into chromosomes.
 
• It regulates essential cellular functions such as growth, metabolism, protein synthesis, and cell division.
 
 
 
• **Plasma Membrane:**
 
 
• The plasma membrane is a semi-permeable structure made of a phospholipid bilayer embedded with proteins.
 
• It regulates the movement of molecules such as nutrients, waste, and ions in and out of the cell.
 
• In animal cells, it is the outermost layer, whereas in plant cells, it is located beneath the cell wall.
 
 
 
• **Cytoplasm:**
 
 
• The cytoplasm is the gel-like substance enclosed within the cell membrane.
 
• It contains organelles such as mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, and Golgi apparatus, as well as cytosol, a fluid component.
 
• It is the site of various cellular processes, including glycolysis and intracellular transport.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Plant vs. Animal Cells:**

 
 
• Plant cells have a rigid cell wall, chloroplasts, and a large central vacuole, which are absent in animal cells.
 
• Animal cells have centrioles and lysosomes, which are not typically found in plant cells.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis:**
 
 
• This process occurs in the chloroplasts of plant cells, where light energy is converted into chemical energy.
 
• The equation for photosynthesis is: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.
 
 
 
• **Endosymbiotic Theory:**
 
 
• Chloroplasts and mitochondria are believed to have originated from free-living prokaryotes through endosymbiosis.
 
• This theory is supported by the presence of their own DNA and double membranes.
